raw_response:
I’m still planting cotton on all 10.1 mu this year. I’ve done this a long time, and on our land cotton is what I know best. Wheat and maize turn fast, but with just two people in the house, cotton fits us better even though picking is tiring. I watch what the other farmers around here do. Most years, if I keep the field clean, put enough fertilizer early, and give water a couple of times when it turns dry, cotton can still make a decent return. I don’t want to spend too much at the start, because cash has to last the whole season, but I also don’t want to save too much on fertilizer and then see weak plants later. So I’ll use a common local cotton seed, put base fertilizer before planting, then topdress once when the plants are growing strong. Since I have a well, I’ll irrigate if the spring is dry and again around flowering if needed. For pests, I won’t spray blindly. I’ll watch the field first, but I do expect to use herbicide and some insecticide because cotton can’t handle weed competition and insects can come fast.
